item.title: Optimizing My Keyboard Layout for a Better Life
item.description: To improve my coding experience, I redesigned my keyboard layout and got rid of my pinky pain. If you're dealing with something similar, read on. Specifically, I adopted virtual layers and Home Row Mods. Over long-term use, I also arrived at a symbol layer design that works well for me. I implemented the design with Kanata, a cross-platform open-source tool. #Dev Auto translated into English by AI.

item.title: Reading the Unreal 5 Garbage Collection Source
item.description: UE 5 uses a mark-sweep garbage collection strategy, with support for incremental collection and cluster-based counting optimizations. This article walks through the UE 5 garbage collection source and summarizes some of its programming patterns. #Dev Auto translated into English by AI.

item.title: Getting Started with Unreal 5 C++ Multiplayer: Resources and Notes
item.description: These are personal notes: a lightweight introductory resource for non-UE developers and people with no multiplayer development experience. Topics include things to watch out for when developing with Rider, commonly used UE C++ classes, garbage collection, and multiplayer networking concepts and features. #Dev Auto translated into English by AI.

item.title: Serializing Components with Bevy Reflection
item.description: Our game uses custom scene files, which means a lot of scene serialization work. This article briefly introduces how to use bevy_reflect to serialize and deserialize Components (to TOML files), including how to insert deserialized reflected values into an Entity. Along the way, I use the custom scene serialization in 猫方块 as an example. #Dev Auto translated into English by AI.

item.title: An Overview of the Bevy Engine's Rendering Architecture
item.description: This article briefly introduces Bevy's rendering architecture, including the directed acyclic graph that manages rendering order, System ordering in the rendering workflow, render phases for different objects, and interactions between the main world and the render world. It uses Bevy Core 3D's rendering implementation as a reference. It also briefly covers how to use Bevy's rendering APIs in everyday development. #Dev Auto translated into English by AI.
